done.why: After a few minutes I'd only walked through empty places and nothing pulled me on. The sword wouldn't move and I had no goal or puzzle to work on.

about: A classic underground-empire cave adventure. You arrive at the bottom of a stair after a dream, with a lantern, and wander dark passages, a sunlit cliff and a shadowy shore. A silver-haired man told me to seek him when I'm worthy, but I never learned how.

moments.note: Walking south into the dark immediately warned of a grue. It was a familiar jolt, but fair.
The Elvish sword in the rock can't be taken. No hint why, so it felt like a dead end.
The sunlit cliff oasis with giant trees was a vivid, memorable spot.
The shadow hills and ocean shore had no visible goal. I didn't know what I was supposed to do.

wished: A clearer short-term goal or nudge toward the old man
A reason to pick up the bread or look at the still figure among the trees

lines.line: A few seedlings from the world above, nurtured by the sunlight and occasional rains, have grown into giant trees, making this a virtual oasis in the desert of the Underground Empire.
lines.why: The best image I saw, and it made the place feel real.

lines.line: Seek me when you feel yourself worthy!
lines.why: The only stated goal, and it's vague.

fun.why: The setting was fine, but I only walked and nothing happened.

engagement.why: Nothing hooked me in the first few minutes, so I left.

difficulty.why: I couldn't tell what to do, so I can't say how hard it is. The sword refusal was a blank wall.

interestingness.why: Some intriguing things were set up (the dream, the sword, the figure hiding among the trees), but I never got to follow any of them.

prose.why: Competent, classic room descriptions, with the cliff oasis standing out.
